official_finding.summary: Cerulean flagged slick 3630124 as class 'Ambiguous' (a human reviewer could not tell if it was oil) and attached a dark vessel, D38.5238724, to it and to four other slicks on the same scene -- corroboration across detections, not a confirmed source.

responsible_parties.name: unidentified dark vessel (Cerulean id D38.5238724)
responsible_parties.role: radar contact with no matching AIS broadcast; estimated length 40 m +/-20%

official_finding.volume_reported: not published by Cerulean for this slick
official_finding.caveat: Cerulean's own reviewer marked this slick 'Ambiguous', not confirmed oil. The claim here is a radar-vs-transponder cross-check, not certainty that this is a spill. A vessel dark to Cerulean's commercial AIS and a vessel absent from our own free NOAA/GFW archive are two independent absences, which is stronger evidence than either alone -- but still an absence, not an identity.

udgam_result.origin_summary: Origin cloud centred at 59.5534° N, 142.7418° W; half the ensemble lands within 1.07 km and nine in ten within 2.29 km. Release window 2023-05-16T08:19:38Z to 2023-05-16T15:49:38Z (age). Stage 3 funnel 14 → 2 → 0 → 0. Abstained: no vessel entered the reconstructed origin during the window 1 radar contact(s) near the slick or origin carried no matching AIS broadcast at acquisition time.

assessment.explanation: UDGAM abstains on every AIS vessel in this case -- correctly: 11 of its 14 AIS-visible 'vessels' were aids to navigation or receiver-telemetry records (five 941* buoys and six 100011xxx records, one of them literally named 'MAJOR BUOY 4'), and once those are filtered by ITU station class, no real vessel enters the reconstructed origin at all. The case's answer is the dark vessel UDGAM surfaces independently: a radar contact with no AIS match, sitting 0.45 km from Cerulean's own dark-vessel contact for this slick. Filtering the buoys out of the AIS pool is also what let this contact surface -- with the buoys still in the pool, UDGAM's radar-vs-AIS cross-check matched the two GFW SAR contacts to buoy transponders instead and reported zero dark vessels.
assessment.what_would_have_helped: A persistence check across more than one satellite pass would turn 'not ruled out as a fixed structure' into a real vessel claim.
